gaps.addiction: Still thin, but better than the first pass. No official list gives a treatment directory: Nevada 211's provider search could not be read, the SNHD page returns truncated, the state DPBH/SAPTA lists are 2015 and 2019 files (not used) and the newer resource guide 404s. The one current official list is Clark County's Opioid Task Force page (12 entries, phones, no addresses, half of them coalitions or national lines). Royal Pages names almost nothing for addiction. Names beyond that still come from ChooseHelp, an aggregator. Several opioid clinics and small agencies could not be confirmed because their own sites were not found. Weighted to private rehabs; free routes found are the Salvation Army and Rescue Mission residential programmes, Crossroads (takes Medicaid), Foundation for Recovery and the harm reduction centre. Scout would still need to find Narcotics Anonymous/Alcoholics Anonymous local lines, SAPTA-funded programmes and Medicaid-accepting clinics.
gaps.children-pregnancy: Still thin. Official lists: the state diaper directory (three general agencies, all fail) and the state Home Visiting providers page (two Clark County providers, both usable) are all that exist; SNHD's maternal-child page returns truncated, the state WIC clinic locator would not show its listings, Nevada 211 gave only the Children's Cabinet (a Reno agency) and Royal Pages is aimed at seniors. WIC clinics were confirmed only on two provider pages. Nothing readable covers child care help, Medicaid prenatal enrolment, school-age children's programmes or pregnancy services other than one clinic. 16 seeds is about all the lists support; Scout would have to find child care assistance, Head Start sites, and further diaper and baby-goods banks.
gaps.clothing-household: Very thin, and still so after the top-up. No official list is a clothing or household-goods directory: Royal Pages mentions clothing only in passing in three entries; Nevada 211's provider search could not be read; the aggregator with Las Vegas clothing closets (needhelppayingbills) returns 403 and the CCSD Family Services clothing page 404s; the Vegas4Locals page lists shops. Most free closets turned out to be limited by rule 3: clients-only (Vegas Stronger), referral-only (Dress for Success) or school-staff access. Only three seeds pass (Rescue Mission, Helping Hands for seniors 60+, Project 150 for high school students), and none gives clothing or furniture to any adult in need on a walk-in basis except the Rescue Mission. St. Vincent de Paul's furniture and clothing programme and the Assistance League could not be checked. Scout would have to find real furniture banks and general clothing closets.
gaps.disability: Best covered of the seven, but not deep. Clark County's Royal Pages 2026-27 and the Reeve Foundation's June 2026 list are current; Royal Pages gives phones and addresses but is aimed at seniors and disabled adults, and the Reeve list is mostly national bodies and Reno agencies, with only a handful of Las Vegas providers. Nevada 211's provider search could not be read. After the top-up 24 seeds is about what these lists support. Hours are missing for most. Not found on any readable list: special education, autism services (the Nevada Autism Center name appeared only as a mis-listing on an addiction aggregator), mobility equipment loans, respite for families, and disability housing beyond Accessible Space. Scout would still have to cover those.
gaps.domestic-violence: The Clark County list is short, so the category is short. The Attorney General's one-page list names only five Clark County programmes (undated), Royal Pages repeats S.A.F.E. House, Nevada 211's provider search could not be read, and the Coalition's member directory could not be reached. The court's protection-order page was the one new official source. Hotlines and the three shelters (SafeNest, S.A.F.E. House, The Shade Tree) are solid and checked on their own pages. Missing: street addresses (shelters are confidential anyway), counselling and support groups for survivors, legal aid for protection orders and divorce, help for male and LGBTQ survivors, and children's programmes. The Immigrant Home Foundation could not be classified. More seeds would need a readable 211 or coalition directory; these lists support 16.
gaps.education: Well covered for adult basic education (ESL, diploma, equivalency): the Henderson Libraries list, the Library District, CSN and CCSD's own site agree, and the four main programmes are checked on their own pages. Thin on everything else under education. Royal Pages' education section is health, legal and financial classes (all fail rule 2). Nothing readable covers children's tutoring, college access, FAFSA help or school enrolment: those names (America Reads and Counts, Andson Foundation, family support centres, Victory Life Church) came from news items and search results with no contacts, so they stay unclear. Nevada 211 could not be read, the state test-centre site and North Las Vegas library site return 403. 16 seeds is what the lists support; Scout would still need to find K-12, college-access and GED-testing locations.
gaps.employment: Official coverage is decent for the main public job services, and checked mostly on the strength of Royal Pages: the state's DETR hub page and PDF both returned 403 again, and Goodwill's and HELP's own sites could not be read, so passes rest on the county list's address and phone. Workforce Connections' own pages say there are 15 Career Hub and Youth Hub locations but their zip-code search does not show results, so only the main office and three state JobConnect offices are recorded. Nevada 211 not read. Not found on any readable list: apprenticeships and trade training other than the Culinary Academy, work-clothing help, jobs for people with a record, day-labour and temp agencies. Hours are missing for most. Scout would need to fill in the 15 hub locations and the training providers.
gaps.financial-assistance: Financial help is covered by Clark County Social Service, HopeLink, JFSA, Lutheran Social Services, Catholic Charities, HELP, ULAN, Salvation Army and the state energy programme, all on official lists (Royal Pages 2026-27 rent and utility section, HUD guidebook). Thin: funding runs out, so most of these are 'when funded' and the county's own fixed-income and eviction rounds were reported closed; the HUD guide includes pandemic-era programmes (RAFT, CHAP) that may no longer exist; United Way's provider list and Nevada 211 give phones and no addresses. Conflicting numbers and addresses for the Salvation Army and the energy assistance office are noted per entry. Entries from the United Way list are unclear because it gives phone only.
gaps.food: Food is well covered by official lists. The Clark County Social Service pantry list (28 Oct 2025, about 57 entries) was transcribed in full; Plentiful (25, mostly the same churches) and Royal Pages 2026-27 (senior meals) added the rest. Most pass on the strength of the county list's phone, address and hours rather than a page of their own; those hours include dated distributions and the list says to call first. Plentiful-only entries are marked unclear because an aggregator alone does not count. Three Square's partner map and Nevada 211's food listings were not readable as text, so its 170+ partner agencies are not captured. Several Henderson and North Las Vegas pantries are reachable but small; Boulder City and Laughlin entries are unclear or fail on reach.
gaps.homeless-services: Front doors are well covered by official sources: coordinated entry (Clark County Social Service, five offices), the City of Las Vegas Courtyard and MORE team, and the VA. The 2023-24 HUD Nevada guidebook adds a full list of shelters for adults, families and youth, which this pass recorded. Thin: Nevada 211's shelter database cannot be read as text, so its listings are not here; the HUD guide is undated and some phones, hours and street addresses conflict with Royal Pages (noted per entry); the coordinated-entry flyer PDF would not download readably. Several shelters have no description or hours on the lists and are passes only on phone and address, so a call is needed. Domestic-violence shelters are in that category's file.
gaps.housing: Housing front doors are well covered: SNRHA, Nevada HAND, Nevada Housing Division's locator, HUD-approved counselling agencies, and the HUD guidebook's lists of subsidized apartments (family, senior, disability). The HUD guide is undated (about 2023-24) and Royal Pages (2026-27) covers senior and disabled housing, so many properties are senior-only or disabled-only; they are marked in the entries. Properties are recorded one per manager or agency, not one per building, for Accessible Space, Nevada HAND and Global Property Management. Clark County's affordable-housing list page and affordablehousingonline's waiting-list page were not re-read in this pass. Nevada 211's housing database cannot be read as text. Vacancies and waiting-list status change, so a call is needed.
gaps.id-recovery: Still very thin. There is no human-maintained Las Vegas list of ID-recovery help. The Social Security card is now covered by Royal Pages (phone and three local offices). The DMV and Southern Nevada Health District vital-records pages returned only headings, errors or truncated text, and dmvnv.com refused the connection, so no DMV or vital-records contact beyond the district's building and main number is confirmed; Nevada 211 results cannot be read as text. Nevada law gives free birth certificates and, from 2026, a free photo ID to people who are homeless, and fee waivers for homeless youth, but this pass found no provider page showing how to get them in Las Vegas (a law summary seen in a search result, not a source for contact details). Scout's own search would have to find those.
gaps.immigration: Thin, and the thinnest of the seven. Immigration has no Royal Pages section and no official Clark County list that could be read: the county's own guide (Families Facing Immigration Issues, which a search summary showed names only Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada and Immigrant Home Foundation) fails the reader on a certificate error, the Nevada Courts non-citizen list returned 403, and Nevada 211's provider database is an interactive search the reader cannot run. Only three independent lists were read (Immigration Advocates, ImmigrationLawHelp, Make the Road's guide of Aug 2025) and they agree: the free front doors are four or five organisations (Legal Aid Center, Immigrant Home Foundation, Nevada Legal Services, Catholic Charities, UNLV clinic with narrow eligibility). The extra names are mostly private law firms, consulates and advocacy groups that fail or are unclear, so the number of passes did not rise. Scout would have to find the DOJ-accredited representatives, church and community legal clinics, and workers' centres directly.
gaps.legal: Short on distinct free providers, because the lists agree. The Nevada Supreme Court list, the county's Royal Pages (which has a Legal Resources section) and the Legal Aid Center's own page all name the same small set: Legal Aid Center, Nevada Legal Services, Southern Nevada Senior Law Program, the two county self-help centres, NDALC and the UNLV clinics. The top-up added four passes, but only NDALC is a new legal-aid agency; the others are county and state self-help or intake lines, and the rest of the new names of the extra names fail the main-service rule (consumer, insurance, guardianship offices). The Clark County Law Library closed to the public on 2 July 2026. Nevada Legal Services' own site would not load (certificate error), so its contact details rest on directory entries. Nevada 211 was tried but its provider database cannot be read; the county's Family Law resource guide and the womenslaw and Nevada Bar lists were not read. Scout would still have to find volunteer-lawyer clinics, church and community legal nights, and record-sealing and name-change help.
gaps.medical-dental-vision: Medical and dental are now covered by an official list: the Southern Nevada Health District's low-cost clinics flyer (Aug 2024) plus Royal Pages 2026-27 and the HUD guide, giving phone and address for about 18 clinics. Still thin: the clinics' own sites rarely loaded, so fees, hours and eligibility come from the lists and need a call; Nevada Health Centers is recorded as separate clinic entries by site, with its other sites on its own page. Vision is still very thin: only Lions SightFirst (online application, PO box) appears on an official list, and no free eye-exam or glasses clinic was found. Dental beyond Nevada Health Centers, First Person Care and the UNLV dental school is also thin (an older 2017 state dental inventory exists but was not read). Nevada 211 results cannot be read as text. BlackHealth-only entries are unclear because they have no street address.
gaps.mental-health: Better after the top-up, but the pass count is limited by what the pages show, not by the lists. The City of Las Vegas 2026-27 Southern Nevada Mental Health directory (printed 16 Sep 2026) is a current official list and gave about 30 names with phone and address; the county's Royal Pages added the senior-focused ones. Many entries are private practices whose pages do not say what an uninsured person pays, so they are unclear, not pass. Nevada 211's category page names service types only; its provider database is interactive and was not readable. The state's SNAMHS locations page returned 404 (details come from the City directory). CCSD's 2023 directory still returns 404 and its 2020 directory turned out to be a health-plan list of individual practitioners, so it was not used. Gaps Scout would still have to fill: who takes uninsured adults at once, Medicaid-accepting clinics beyond the few named, peer-run and crisis walk-in sites, and children's services.
gaps.reentry-support: Reentry is still thin. No official Las Vegas or Clark County list of community reentry providers was found: the Nevada DOC reentry page describes the programme inside prisons and names no local providers; Clark County's Royal Pages is for seniors; the HUD guide has no reentry section. The one list of reentry providers is ProbationInfo.org (an undated national aggregator), whose eight Las Vegas entries are mostly general social services, so they are unclear or fail rule 2. CareerOneStop's finder and Nevada 211 could not be read as text. HOPE for Prisoners is the only pass and carries a 2026 governance concern (Nevada Independent). The state's P.R.I.D.E. programme and the NDOC reentry guide were not found in a readable form. Scout's own search would have to find ex-offender employment, parole-office, record-sealing and transitional-housing programmes.
gaps.seniors: Much better after the top-up. The Royal Pages 2026-27 is a current official directory of exactly this category, with a Senior Recreation, Food, Respite, Home Maintenance, Advocates and Legal sections; the City of Las Vegas 2026-27 directory added the county's Senior Advocate Program. Senior centres, meal sites, state advocacy lines and home-repair programmes now have phone and address from an official list, and the county's own page did not load for most. The county, city and Henderson park pages still failed, so no hours were confirmed for the senior centres, and none of the centres' own pages was read. The long list of private home-care agencies in the Royal Pages is unclear on cost and who they serve; about 13 are recorded and the rest are named in one summary entry. Nevada 211's provider database cannot be read. Scout would still need current hours, meal days and eligibility for each centre, and sliding-fee or free in-home help.
gaps.transportation: Still thin for people in need who are not seniors, disabled or veterans. The Royal Pages (a Transportation section) and the state veterans pages gave the new names, and they cover seniors, disabled riders and veterans well. For everyone else the lists say almost nothing: bus passes sit inside HELP of Southern Nevada's emergency help, and nothing names help with gas, car repair, ride-share vouchers or rides for people under 60 who are not disabled. RTC's site (paratransit, reduced fare) returns 403 to the reader, so those two entries rest on the official-list entries, not RTC's own page. Nevada 211's provider database cannot be read. Scout would have to find rides for working-age adults, free bus-pass programmes, and church and community ride ministries.
gaps.utilities-phone-internet: Phone and internet are well covered by the Clark County Broadband list, which names every provider but shows no price or low-income terms for most, so the extra names are recorded as fail (commercial companies). Utility-bill help is the thin part. The Royal Pages gave the real local front doors (HELP of Southern Nevada, Catholic Charities, Jewish Family Service, Lutheran Social Services, ULAN, Salvation Army, county senior funds, Project REACH), and Southwest Gas's own page confirms Energy Share runs through HELP, but none of their own pages describes current funding, and several pantries and churches give small bill help that no list captured. NV Energy's page gave only headings, the EOB 2021 list returned 403, the needhelppayingbills aggregator was not read, the Las Vegas Valley Water District's assistance page returned 404, and Nevada 211's provider database cannot be read. Water-bill help is still missing. Scout would need current funding status and water and sewer help.
gaps.veterans: Better, but the local nonprofit layer is still thin. The City of Las Vegas 2026-27 directory (veterans services section), the county Royal Pages 2026-27 (a Veteran Services section) and the VA's own pages gave the main front doors: VA, Vet Centers, state office, crisis line, Salvation Army, homeless-veteran services. The state's Southern Nevada resources page returned 404, and the only broader list (Senator Rosen's guide) is from 2022, so its posts and small transport names are unclear. Veterans Village (SHARE) now has a consistent phone in two official lists but two different addresses, and its own page returned 404, so it stays unclear; vvlv.org was not used. U.S. VETS and Key Foundation also need a call. Nevada 211 was not tried for this category and its database cannot be read. Scout would still have to find veteran emergency aid, legal help, and current phone and address for the housing providers.
